title: Manipulating and Interrogating Spatial Transcriptomics
text:
Mounting evidence correlates the dysregulation of spatial mRNA organization to an increasing number of
diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), fragile X syndrome (FXS), and spinal muscular atrophy
(SMA). However, the regulatory mechanism and pathological consequences of spatial RNA organization have
only been explored for a limited fraction of mRNAs, due to a lack of technologies that allow for tracking and
manipulating the subcellular localization of endogenous mRNAs. We develop a transformative framework
including several technologies: single-molecule, real-time RNA monitoring (RNA-LiveFISH), manipulation of any
endogenous mRNA(s) for spatial localization on a large scale (CRISPR-TO), and related machine learning
algorithms, and we will apply the framework to gain new insights into the functional roles of spatial RNA
organization in axon development and guidance in primary neurons and explore the approach of modulating
mRNA localization as a therapeutic strategy to treat spinal muscular atrophy.

title: Hypoxia's role in regulating stressed hematopoietic stem cells
text: Isolation and processing hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) in the hypoxia condition strikingly improve numbers and functionalities of HSCs. Here, we propose to study the functions of p38 MAPK/Nrf2/Bach1 pathway in the hypoxia condition in the context of Fanc-/- HSCs. We will also develop a Spacer-Nick gene correction system along with inhibition of p38 pathway to restore the functions of Fanc-/- HSCs.

title: Basic Cancer Center - Cancer Center at Illinois
text: The Cancer Center at Illinois (CCIL) promotes fundamental advances in basic science and engineering for cancer research, accelerating their development into new technologies and treatments to improve care. Two complementary programs and three shared resources support activities that span the career arcs of diverse cancer researchers. Guided by a Strategic Plan and effective leadership, CCIL coordinates relevant institutional resources, integrates educational and mentoring programs, and forms translational partnerships to provide new opportunities in advancing its “Discovery-to-Use” paradigm.

title: Mechanisms and Treatments for Right Ventricular-related Inherited Arrhythmias Using Chamber-specific iPSC Models and Engineered tRNA Therapy
text:
The right ventricle of the heart can be a source of life-threatening arrhythmias in a number of acquired and
inherited forms of heart disease. Brugada syndrome is an inherited arrhythmia syndrome associated with
arrhythmias originating in the right ventricle. Human induced pluripotent stem cells from patients with Brugada
syndrome will be used to investigate the underlying mechanisms leading to arrhythmias and test an innovative
therapeutic approach.

title: Lineage and functional consequences of clonally expanded microglia in AD brain
text:
This study will investigate how genetic changes that occur during a person’s lifetime could affect immune cells
in the brain and contribute to the development of Alzheimer’s disease. By understanding how these changes
influence response to brain inflammation, this work will advance our knowledge of how aging impacts brain
health. In the long term, the findings could help identify new ways to detect, prevent, or treat Alzheimer’s and
related neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Research Track Radiology Residency
text:
The University of Pennsylvania seeks to continue its highly successful physician-scientist
training program for radiologists in the form of the Research Track Radiology Residency.
This program is motivated by rapid advances in imaging technology and methodology
and the need for radiology physician-scientists who are equipped to translate these
advances to the clinic. The ongoing success of the Program's trainees, evidenced by
academic radiology faculty appointments, NIH funding and radiology research leadership
roles, support the continuation of this program and the innovations in the proposed
renewal designed for the evolving landscape of radiology research.

title: HIV-1 membrane fusion and inhibition
text:
In this project, we will capitalize on advanced technologies to examine how HIV-1 enters a host cell and to dissect
the mechanisms of entry inhibition. The goal is to transform our understanding of early steps of HIV-1 infection
and to inform the design of novel antiviral inhibitors and vaccines.

title: Characterizing neurogenic progenitors in the adult intestine
text:
The adult enteric nervous system contains neuronal progenitors that can be leveraged for regenerative cell
therapy to treat neurointestinal diseases, but the pathways that mediate the neurogenic response in the
postnatal intestine are unknown. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesize that inflammatory mediators
released by intestinal macrophages act on specific populations of enteric glial cells to activate their
differentiation to a neuronal lineage. In this proposal, we will determine the role of activated macrophages and
their inflammatory cytokines in glial-derived neurogenesis, examine the role of Sox2 and Sox10 transcription
factors in this process, and characterize the phenotypic diversity of the glial-derived neurons that are
generated.

title: Elucidating the Role of the Thousand and One Kinases in Retinal Ganglion Cell Death
text:
We previously identified dual leucine zipper kinase (DLK) and leucine zipper kinase (LZK) as the master
regulators of the signaling pathway that mediates cell death following axon injury as observed in optic
neuropathies like glaucoma. Using a clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)-based
screen in primary retinal ganglion cells, we identified the thousand and one kinases 1 and 2 (TAOK1/2) to be
previously unknown participants in the DLK/LZK signaling and thus, promising neuroprotective targets. In this
proposal, we develop and use novel adenovirus and adeno-associated virus/CRISPR vectors and
pharmacological means to test the hypothesis that TAOK1/2 work as regulators of the DLK/LZK/JNK signaling
axis and mediate neuronal cell death in rodent and human in vitro models of optic neuropathy.

title: Harnessing single cell RNA sequencing and integrative bioinformatics to identify precision therapeutics for dermatomyositis
text:
The majority of children and adults with dermatomyositis (DM) still experience long-term functional impairment
with modern treatments. Drug repositioning is an untapped opportunity to identify existing treatments that work
in a precise manner for complex autoimmune diseases, like DM. Using a combination of single-cell RNA
sequencing, computational drug repurposing, and ex-vivo cell culture assays, we will identify existing
compounds that perturb DM-associated molecular networks in DM-associated cell types with the long-term
goal of improving health outcomes through the identification of precision medicine treatments.

title: Single cell investigation of co-evolution in cancer cells and host cell immune microenvironment
text:
Although new advances in the field of cancer immunology and genomics have transformed the
way people are thinking about the importance of immunotherapy in cancer treatment, remaining
questions of current immunotherapy are how the cancer cells and microenviroment immune
cells evolve during therapy and how to increase the cancer patient response rate. Here, we
propose to use novel single cell/genomics technologies to understand both the changes in
cellular circuitry underlying malignancy initiation, progression, and transformation, and the co-
evolving changes in the tumor microenvironment. These aims will be pursued in the context of
existing NCI-funded research programs in the Translational Immunogenomics Laboratory
directed by Dr. Catherine Wu at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

title: Clinical Validation of DystoniaNet Deep Learning Platform for Diagnosis of Isolated Dystonia
text:
The proposed research aims to conduct retrospective and prospective studies for clinical validation of a
DystoniaNet deep learning platform for the diagnosis of isolated dystonia. The proposed research is relevant to
public health because the translation and implementation of a robustly validated, objective and accurate
diagnostic approach of isolated dystonia is expected to have a significant positive impact on the clinical
management of this disorder. Thus, the proposed research is relevant to the part of NIH’s mission that pertains
to developing and applying fundamental knowledge that will help to reduce the burdens of human disability.

title: Structure-Guiding Tools to Study the Role of Choline in the Development of Congenital Hydrocephalus
text:
Mutations in the blood brain barrier (BBB) choline transporter FLVCR2, and the related choline and ethanolamine
transporter, FLVCR1 (expressed in brain neuroprogenitor cells, NPCs), cause congenital hydrocephalus (CH).
While both proteins transport choline and can also regulate intracellular heme, the mechanisms linking defective
choline transport and cellular heme metabolism to CH are unknown. Our goal is to develop new tools to address
these questions at a molecular level.

title: Deciphering Mechanisms of Limb Malformations Caused by Noncoding Variants In Vivo
text:
Limb malformations are the second most common congenital abnormality and are becoming increasingly linked
to rare noncoding variants in transcriptional enhancers, short DNA sequences that activate gene expression.
Yet, the disease mechanisms by which these rare noncoding variants disrupt normal limb development remain
unclear. In this proposal, I will use novel transgenic mouse technology and single-cell epigenomics to determine
the genetic factors mediating the unique susceptibility of limb-specific enhancers to pathogenic noncoding
variants.

title: Imaging
text: PROJECT SUMMARY—Imaging Core (Core E) Brain imaging plays a critical role in research and care of dementia. The Imaging Core of this PPG on frontotemporal dementia (FTD) has facilitated scientific discovery since its initiation in 2002. Brain imaging has been used by this PPG to characterize different forms of FTD, support diagnosis, and advance knowledge about a variety of brain functions that are particularly affected in FTD, including executive control, social and emotional behavior, speech, and langauge. To achieve these goals, we have used a variety of imaging modalities including structural MRI; diffusion MRI (dMRI); task-free functional MRI (tf-fMRI); and FDG, amyloid, and tau PET. Over the last few years, this core has also focused on the development of longitudinal processing pipelines for multiple imaging modalities to facilitate tracking disease over time. In the next cycle of the PPG, the Imaging Core will continue to support novel uses of brain imaging to validate new assessments of emotion and language (in Project 1: Language and Emotions); develop biological markers of specific proteinopathies (Project 2: Molecular Biomarkers); understand the factors that influence caregiver health (Project 3: Caregiver Health); and understand cognitive resilience, variation in rates of decline, and develop a new clinical trials meaure (Project 4: FTD Heterogeneity). All of these projects will utilize cross-sectional and longitudinal imaging data generated by this core, in particular structural MRI, dMRI, and tf-fMRI. To support this work, the Imaging Core will pursue the following aims: Aim 1: Collection and archiving of images and maintainenance of an image database. We will collect and manage the following MRI sequences in patients with the behavioral variant of FTD; the nonfluent, semantic, and logopenic variants of primary progressive aphasia; corticobasal syndrome; progressive supranuclear palsy-Richardson’s syndrome; and Alzheimer’s diseas;, and in controls: MP-RAGE, FLAIR, dMRI, ASL-perfusion tf-fMRI, and T2-weighted MRI. We will also acquire 18F-PI2620 and 18F-Florbetaben PET scans in patients for whom clinical features and blood biomarkers for AD are inconsistent. Aim 2: Extraction of imaging data to create cross-sectional estimates of structure, function, and molecular pathology. We will generate regional estimates of volume and structural connectivity coinciding with the baseline visit for each participant. Aim 3: Creation of longitudinal MRI-based change data. We will generate regional estimates of volume and structural connectivity coinciding with each visit in each participant, and voxelwise maps of longitudinal change in volume and white matter integrity. Aim 4: Data archiving and analytical consultation. We will work with PPG investigators and staff and other researchers at our center to incorporate imaging data into their analyses.

title: Investigating the anti-tumor roles of tumor-draining lymph nodes in renal cell carcinoma
text:
Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells play critical roles in anti-tumor immunity, but they become exhausted in the solid tumor
microenvironment and lose the ability to kill cancer cells. Studies in mice demonstrate that stem-like CD8+ T
cells in the tumor-draining lymph nodes (tdLNs) play a key role in sustaining anti-tumor immunity, but how this
translates to human solid tumors remains unclear. This project aims to leverage complementary human and
mouse models of renal cell carcinoma to investigate how CD8+ T cell subsets and tdLNs drive anti-tumor
immunity, advancing our understanding of these mechanisms and informing the development of adoptive cell
therapies.

title: CLEC16A-Driven Regulation of Astrocytes
text:
Astrocytes play important roles in central nervous system (CNS) physiology and pathology. Indeed, specific
astrocyte subsets contribute to the pathology of neurologic diseases including multiple sclerosis (MS), but little
is known about the control of disease-promoting astrocyte responses and their therapeutic targeting. In this
project we use novel genomic and interactomic tools, animal models and clinical samples to investigate the
regulation of pathogenic astrocyte responses and subsets in MS, and approaches for their therapeutic targeting.

title: Technologies to study and control patterning and differentiation in multicellular development, a case study for multilayered arterial wall of controlled thickness
text:
Naturally evolved genetic networks based on signals and receptors are implicated in the normal development of
embryos and adult homeostasis of organs like for example arterial vessels and, when disrupted, can cause
developmental abnormalities, cancers, and degenerative diseases. To cure diseases, we need to understand
how genes control signaling networks at multiple scales, and how these networks drive cells to form coherent
functional tissues and organs or dysfunctional disease states. We propose to use approaches of synthetic
biology to control signals and receptors that would affect cell-cell signaling, with application to the construction
of a multilayered arterial tissue, to increase our understanding of cell decision-making in multicellular contexts
and to construct more realistic model systems.

title: Cutaneous biomarkers of pediatric non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
text:
Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the most common liver disease in the world, affecting 8% of all
children and 34% or more of those with obesity. This study will determine and validate the role of skin surface
lipids, which can be collected using painless tape stripping, as novel, non-invasive biomarkers of disease
presence and severity in youth with NAFLD. The results have the potential to revolutionize clinical practice and
to enhance therapeutic discovery, which is currently limited by the need for invasive liver biopsies to accurately
detect and stage disease severity.

title: Imaging intracerebral and systemic T cell immunity in patients with Alzheimer's disease using 18F-F-AraG
text:
(Relevance)
The development of an imaging method for noninvasive detection of aberrant T cell activity in
patients with Alzheimer disease is crucial for enhancing our understating of the role of adaptive
immunity in the development and progression of Alzheimer disease. This technique has the
potential to pave the way for new immunotherapy approaches and fundamentally change the
paradigm by which Alzheimer's disease is treated and managed.
